text: Keep the dependency direction host -> engine <- command modules, with the host abstraction (`PSHost`) as the only UI contract.

Split the engine into separately packaged components (language core, runtime, remoting, formatting, help) so enterprise deployments can omit unneeded subsystems and shrink the attack surface; the observable language behavior stays unchanged.
Provide a one-call embedding entry that takes an initial session state (as `ConsoleShell.Start` does).
Build with standard `dotnet` tooling and MSBuild props only, with version computed from one tag plus an explicit override, instead of an orchestration module needing an installed shell.

Keep the two preprocessor families (`UNIX`/`CORECLR`) out of the language core by isolating platform code behind an interface; PowerShell's use of `IsWindows` to drive `DefineConstants` spreads `#if UNIX` through the engine.
Pin a single package feed and commit lock files; PowerShell pins one feed but ships no lock files.
Generate resource accessors and type catalogs at build time with small console tools that are themselves part of the repository (`ResGen`, `TypeCatalogGen`).
Use declarative pipeline templates plus a thin script layer; keep package-format code behind a single `Start-Package`-style entry with a closed format list as `Start-PSPackage` does.
Pin third-party workflows by commit SHA and run dependency review, CodeQL and Scorecard on every change.
Validate signed payloads against an explicit allow-list signer policy before publishing.
Adopt warnings-as-errors with an explicit analyzer severity file from day one.
Write the breaking-change contract before the first release and apply it to language behavior, cmdlet parameters and protocols alike.
Keep platform differences behind interfaces rather than `#if` blocks across the engine (PowerShell has `UNIX` in 122 files).
Use the hot-path rules (no LINQ, no `params`, pre-sized collections) only inside the interpreter and runtime core, and let a profiler decide elsewhere.
Keep a parser-selected `Mode` (Command / Expression / TypeName / Signature) on a pull-style tokenizer; initial mode Command; each switch restored in `finally`.
Treat `-name` as a parameter in Command mode and as dash-operator-or-parameter in Expression mode; recognize keywords only in Command/Signature mode.
Reproduce the generic-token rule in Command mode: operator characters and non-terminators glue into one word, with the exact terminator set (`ForceStartNewToken`).

Implement rescan with an explicit snapshot (position + mode) instead of resyncing from a token, but keep the one-token-lookahead contract so a mode switch re-reads the peeked token. Why: same observable behavior, simpler to reason about.
Number literal grammar: suffix before multiplier, multiplier needs `b`, two's-complement hex/binary, int→long→decimal→double promotion.
Pre-scan `$(...)` inside strings with a tokenizer-aware scan (quotes and comments), not paren counting alone. Why: avoids the early-`)` edge case; observable behavior for valid scripts is identical.
Leave `#requires` processing and signature lookalike detection out of the tokenizer (move to a later phase or omit); replace with a dedicated pragma pass if the owner wants it.
Hand-written recursive descent with exactly one token of lookahead; the parser, not the tokenizer, owns Command/Expression mode and restores it after each rule.
At a statement start try an expression in Expression mode first (assignment target or first pipeline element), then fall back to a command.

Parse binary operators with an operand stack and operator stack driven by a per-operator precedence level, all left-associative; comma binds tighter than every binary operator; ternary and assignment sit above.
Do not require a terminator after block statements; skip optional newlines and semicolons between statements, and stop pipelines at newline, `;`, `)`, `}`, `&&`, `||`, `&`.

Collect errors with de-duplication, return error AST nodes and recover by pretending closers or skipping to a sync token; mark errors at end-of-script as incomplete input so the REPL can continue the line.
Keep stack-depth protection but replace the retry-on-new-thread with a fixed nesting limit that reports `ScriptTooComplicated`. Why: same observable error, deterministic and testable.
Do not perform filesystem access or runspace creation while parsing (`using assembly` resolution, `configuration`); resolve such directives in a later phase.
One class per construct, get-only properties, constructor invariants that throw on invalid combinations, and parent links set exactly once.
Provide a pre-order visitor with `Continue`/`SkipChildren`/`StopVisit` and a post-visit hook that fires on every exit path.
Keep error nodes (`ErrorStatementAst`, `ErrorExpressionAst`) that hold partially parsed children so tooling works on broken scripts.
Treat hashtable values as statements and keep `PipelineChainAst` left-nested with a plain `PipelineAst` on the right, as the parser produces them.

Use one visitor family with a default `Visit` for new nodes instead of two families gated by "v2" interfaces. Why: the v1/v2 split exists for source compatibility with external visitors, which a new shell does not have.

Make type names (`ITypeName`) plain syntax objects resolved lazily by the type system, with a cache owned by the resolver. Why: keeps the AST free of reflection state while keeping the observable `[type]` resolution.
Do not store compiler caches (`TupleIndex`, `RuntimeUsingIndex`, `TypeDefinitionAst.Type`) or assignment-code-generation methods on AST nodes; keep them in side tables keyed by node.

Provide an allow-list "literal data" evaluator (no commands, no member calls, no binary operators, node and key caps) for manifests and data sections, evaluated without the compiler. Why: same observable safety as `SafeGetValue`, without depending on the compiler for unary/convert nodes.

Keep semantic rules (duplicate parameters, loop-control placement, assignment targets, attribute-argument constants, hashtable duplicate keys, `$using` shape) as a post-parse pass that reports into the parser's error list.
Validate `data` sections with an allow-list checker and refuse operators flagged as disallowed in restricted mode.
Resolve type names in a fixed order (script types, accelerators, assemblies, user accelerators, `using namespace` retries) and cache results per (name, state).

Do slot allocation as a separate pass with a definite-assignment analysis, but start with a simple rule (slot only if assigned before every read, never for non-local scopes) and keep a dynamic-lookup fallback. Why: same observable variable behavior with far less code than the flow-graph analysis.
Report all class-definition errors in the semantic pass instead of at first compile. Why: same error set, earlier and deterministic.
Do not run module lookups (`Get-Module -ListAvailable`) while parsing `using module`; record the directive and resolve it in a later phase.

Start with a tree-walking evaluator over the AST that implements the protocols of §6 and [IR-SPEC.md](IR-SPEC.md) §5; add an IR later only if profiling demands it. Why: same observable behavior, far less code than a 6,600-line expression-tree compiler.
Implement statement output as writes to the current output pipe with temporary capture pipes for conditions, assignments, `$()` and `@()`.
Keep statement-level error handling with resume-at-next-statement, rethrowing flow-control signals untouched.
Match `try/catch/finally` semantics: typed handlers in order, `$_` bound to an `ErrorRecord`, `finally` runs after `return`, cleanup runs even for a stopped pipeline.
`switch` evaluates every clause per item; `foreach` wraps a non-enumerable in a one-element sequence; loop labels match case-insensitively with an empty label matching any loop.
Cache parsed script blocks by (file, text) but share only immutable compiled data between clones. Why: PowerShell clears the whole cache at 1024 entries; use an LRU instead.
Do not run an AMSI scan, suspicious-pattern hashing or admin-block checks as part of compilation in MicroteamShell; add a separate policy hook if needed.
Define behavior once, in the evaluator and the protocols, never per execution strategy; if two strategies are ever added, test them differentially.
`finally` must run for every exit (return, break, continue, throw) and flow-control signals must never be swallowed by catch-all handlers.

Do not port the typed arithmetic/comparison instruction families or the DLR-derived interpreter; they are unreachable or defective for PowerShell. Replace with the evaluator's own numeric semantics from CONVERSION-RULES (planned T28).

A tree-walker over the AST can replace the IR, provided it implements the protocols in §5 (output pipe, `$?`, error-action resume, positions, flow control). Why: the observable behavior is defined by the protocols, not by expression trees.
Statements write to an output pipe; assignments, `++`/`--` and conditions do not; capturing output swaps the current pipe and restores it in a `finally`.
Wrap each statement so that non-flow-control exceptions go to the error-action policy and execution continues with the next statement when the policy says so.

Represent break/continue/return as control-flow signals inside the evaluator, and as exceptions only when crossing function or script-block boundaries. Why: PowerShell uses labels in-lambda and exceptions across lambdas; a tree-walker has no lambdas but still crosses script-block calls.
Keep a per-statement sequence-point index in the call frame so errors and the debugger can report positions.

Start with a tree-walking evaluator only; it is a valid first tier (all observable behavior is defined by the IR semantics, not by the JIT). `INFERENCE`: PowerShell's tiers are equivalent by design ([EQUIVALENCE-SPEC.md](EQUIVALENCE-SPEC.md)).

If a second tier is ever added, trigger it by call count with a deterministic (synchronous) policy first, and keep results independent of the tier. Why: PowerShell's asynchronous promotion makes tier choice nondeterministic.

Keep two variable-storage strategies visible in the design: fast slots when the scope is private and analyzable, dynamic lookup when debugging, dot-sourcing, or `AllScope`/`New-Variable`-style access is possible.

Do not copy background (thread-pool) compilation of hot loops with an in-place instruction replacement; it needs the interpreter and compiled code to share frames exactly. Replace by an explicit, synchronous optimization step if a loop optimizer is wanted.
Treat CIM/WMI as an optional adapter module, not part of the base command set.
Leave OS-specific diagnostics out of the initial command set and offer them as optional modules.
Keep path- and item-commands provider-agnostic (the same verb set for files, registry, environment, functions) and let providers declare capabilities.
Route OS-level actions (process, service, computer) through an explicit capability so they can be denied per policy.
Split the utility set by risk: pure data/formatting commands vs code-loading (`Add-Type`, `Invoke-Expression`) and network commands, so a policy can grant them independently.
Implement object-manipulation commands against the public cmdlet base-class API only, so third-party modules can replace them.
Keep transcription as a host service behind a command pair, so non-console hosts can supply their own sink.
Use the platform's standard structured-logging/ETW abstractions (`EventSource`, OpenTelemetry) instead of a private ETW wrapper.
Keep GUI helpers behind a late-bound host service (reflection or plug-in) so the engine never references UI assemblies.
Expose signature validation and policy queries as ordinary commands over a policy service so audit tooling can use the same API as users.
Do not rely on `SecureString` cmdlets as a secrets boundary; replace with an OS-keychain-backed secret type (see Phase 5 blueprint).
Do not carry the WSMan command family into the new shell; remoting transport should be pluggable behind one session abstraction.
Register built-in commands from a declarative table (name -> implementing type -> help) as PowerShell does, but generate the table from attributes at build time so it cannot drift from the classes.
Keep `ForEach-Object`/`Where-Object` as engine-level commands with direct pipeline access so script-block pipelines do not pay module-load or binding overhead.
